findings.conclusion: WaitRig initializes the state actually used by the Rig/GccRig/RpmhRig/DisplayRig helpers. Register routing, command/status offsets, clock_step replies, persistent QMP line framing and ID matching, asynchronous IRQ draining, and short socket paths are consistent with the pinned helpers.

Non-response commands distinguish ISSUED from COMPLETE at WAIT bits 0 and 15. Resource/Clock state and real IRQ observations corroborate the register checks. Rejected BUSY writes at 400 ns retain the original deadline, tested with 599 ns then 1 ns; CMD_ENABLE high bits and unknown resources retain their strict behavior.

Reset uses a nonzero GCC L witness and query-status as an asynchronous RESET barrier, then checks state, diagnostics and absence of delayed completion. The isolated machine configuration has GCC boot configuration disabled. The paused normal-TCG case reads QOM only and does not execute cont or a QTest-only Clock getter.

The independent main payload expression is 40 + 4*(17 + 8*346) + 98*84 + 8 = 19420 bytes; the new subsection is 24 bytes (>IQIII). The pending source has no completed resource vote, so the literal all-zero voter oracle is applicable. SysBus lacks get_dev_path, which supports the bare device migration section name used by this instance.

The source stops, performs two pure-QOM observations, saves and checks completion. The target prewarms different diagnostics and RAM, aligns its QTest clock for the unchanged parent absolute-deadline format, then checks QOM and RAM before RPMh MMIO. A subsequent 599 ns / 1 ns sequence observes actual Clock/resource/IRQ changes before the first RPMh MMIO, so that read cannot repair missing timer restoration.

Both profile mismatches and both corruptions require actual destination exit 1 plus specific model and migration-load diagnostics. Each corruption changes exactly one bit in one byte of the subsection (policy 1 to 0, or last voter 3 to 7), preserves all other file bytes, and retains the original source hash. Process cleanup follows the failure assertions.
